**Where the charter-global defects cost this task.** Both bear on this world, and each hands the

**F-1 demonstrated (undeclared override: filed versus accepted claim).**
The order `c73faeec-…` carries `protection_claim_reference: "CL-330871"`. In
`initial_state.protection_ledger`, CL-330871 appears exactly once —
`protection_entry_id: 7bdd809f-…`, `event_type: "protection_claim_filed"`, `posted_date: "2026-09-05"`,
`claim_outcome: "not_applicable"`. There is **no** `protection_claim_settled` and **no**
`protection_claim_denied` row for CL-330871. (The world does contain both for other claims:
CL-291445 settled 2024-08-02, CL-318902 denied 2026-02-05 — so the seed deliberately distinguishes
the three states.)

- Reading A, extended rule: "a protection claim that stands filed against the covered piece and has
  not been refused" — CL-330871 qualifies → apply a credit of **1587.01** (derived below).
- Reading B, inherited base sentence: "Where no protection claim has been accepted the desk does not
  take the amount off in anticipation of one" — CL-330871 has not been accepted → apply nothing.

Reading B is not merely a refusal to make write 1; it propagates. With no coverage credit,
`coverage_taken_off = 0`, so at write 2 `net_bench_total = 2757.30 − 197.60 = 2559.70`
(rather than 972.69); `covered_step_pct` is still 9 because `allowance_left` 2800.00 ≥ 2559.70;
`allowance = RND(2559.70 × 37 / 100, 2) = 947.09`; `uplifted = RND(947.09 × 1.25, 2) = 1183.86`;
ceiling = **3743.56** (rather than 1422.57). At write 3, `base_amount = RND(3743.56 × 22 / 100, 2) = 823.58`;
`relieved = RND((823.58 + 185.00) × 90 / 100, 2) = 907.72`; `cap = RND(3743.56 × 40 / 100, 2) = 1497.42`;
surcharge = **907.72** (rather than 448.17).

Two clauses of the policy in force therefore reach different conclusions in this same situation, and
the scored quantity of every one of this task's three writes moves. `SOURCE-POLICY RED`.
*Affected artifact and location:* `service.extended.yaml`, `extended_policies[0]
service_ext_claim_coverage_credit`, `overwrite` (incomplete) and `rule` (first sentence); and, through
the chain, the scored `covered_amount`, `authorized_ceiling` and `surcharge_amount` of this task.

**F-9 demonstrated (undeclared override: the out-of-hours charge).**
Nothing in this task's world records that the bench was held open out of hours: `service_orders`

- Reading B, inherited base sentence "it is charged only where the bench was actually held open":

### problem_chain

Walked out from the policy and the world alone, starting from the root problem the customer raises.

**The customer raises exactly one problem.** `user_scenario`: *"I'm trying to find out whether there's
any way of getting my ring finished sooner - our anniversary is on the third of October and I'd rather
not spend it without the ring."* That is expedited handling, and nothing else. She names no
prerequisite: she does not mention the protection claim, the coverage credit, the ceiling, or any
"do I need to sort something out first?" steer. The two disclosures she can make are both
agent-initiated and passive — *"Only if the agent asks her about coverage or membership does she
mention that there is a care plan on the ring… she cannot quote a number from either and she does not
raise them herself"* — and neither names a problem to be resolved. The authorisation hand-over is
likewise conditional on the agent: *"If the agent tells her there is a figure she has to agree to
before the bench can carry on, she wants to hear the figure first; once she has heard it she says yes,
and when the agent hands the step over to her she carries it out herself."* She issues no second item
of work (no document to send, no address, no statement), and she closes exactly where the last write
lands: *"Once the agent tells her the expedited handling has been put on the order and the ring will
be finished ahead of the third, she is satisfied."*

**Nodes and edges, as the policy and the world yield them.**

Root: `service_ext_expedited_surcharge` (the customer's request). Its rule carries one prerequisite
sentence — *"The charge for expedited handling is priced only after the work order carries an
authorisation the customer has confirmed on the day the expedited handling is taken on."*

- **Edge E1 — root → `service_ext_revised_authorization`, `kind: value_input`, `gate: ceiling`.**
  *Why false at the opening:* `initial_state.service_intake` holds exactly one row,
  `a6869385-f33c-4834-918e-e0d29d79b153`, with `request_status: "customer_confirmed"`,
  `authorized_amount: 3200.0`, `effective_date: "2026-06-25"`. `frozen_time` is 2026-09-17, so the
  only confirmed authorisation on this work order is effective on a date that is not the handling
  date. The state the sentence waits on does not hold.
  *Which policy brings it about:* read as a reader must — the sentence names no tool. Of the five
  extended rules, only `service_ext_revised_authorization` describes producing a ceiling a customer
  agrees ("The ceiling a customer agrees for work already at the bench is worked out on…"), and only
  `confirm_authorized_ceiling_b1b9df84` writes `request_status="customer_confirmed"` to
  `service_intake`. One reading.
  *Load-bearing run:* skip write 2 and replay write 3 unchanged. `ceiling` then resolves to the only
  confirmed row, 3200.00, giving `base_amount = RND(3200.00 × 22/100, 2) = 704.00`,
  `relieved = RND((704.00 + 185.00) × 90/100, 2) = 800.10`, `cap = RND(3200.00 × 40/100, 2) = 1280.00`,
  surcharge **800.10** instead of 448.17. The edge bears weight.

`service_ext_revised_authorization`'s own rule carries one prerequisite sentence — *"The ceiling is
fixed only after every amount a protection claim answers for on the work order stands recorded
against the priced line it answers for."*

- **Edge E2 — `service_ext_revised_authorization` → `service_ext_claim_coverage_credit`,
  `kind: value_input`, `gate: coverage_taken_off`.**
  *Why false at the opening:* of the ten rows in `initial_state.service_ledger`, none has
  `event_type: "service_coverage_applied"`. The six rows on order `c73faeec-…` are three
  `service_labor_charged` plus one more, two `service_goodwill_discount_applied`, one
  `service_payment_received` and one `service_quality_check_logged`. No credit stands recorded against
  any priced line. The state does not hold.
  *Which policy brings it about:* only `service_ext_claim_coverage_credit`'s rule describes a credit
  "taken off the order as a single credit recorded against one priced line", and only
  `apply_claim_coverage_f28c459e` creates a `service_coverage_applied` row. One reading.
  *Load-bearing run:* skip write 1 and replay writes 2 and 3 unchanged. `coverage_taken_off = 0` →
  `net_bench_total = 2559.70` → ceiling **3743.56** → surcharge **907.72**, against 1422.57 and
  448.17. The edge bears weight.

`service_ext_claim_coverage_credit` has `prerequisite: []`; its rule carries no ordering sentence
waiting on anything, and every input it needs stands in the seed. The walk terminates.

**Derived tree** (identical in shape to the `prerequisite` field of the charter, which is the whole
point of deriving it independently):

```
service_ext_expedited_surcharge          (root; customer's request; agent write)
   └─[value_input: ceiling]─> service_ext_revised_authorization   (customer's own write)
          └─[value_input: coverage_taken_off]─> service_ext_claim_coverage_credit  (agent write)
```

n = 2 prerequisite problems; `value_input` edges = 2, floor `max(n−1,1) = 1` — met. No cycle: the
chain is linear with no back-edge.

**Topological order:** `service_ext_claim_coverage_credit` → `service_ext_revised_authorization` →
`service_ext_expedited_surcharge`. This is forced, not chosen: E2's gate is an input to write 2 and
E1's gate is an input to write 3.

**Parallel edges / terminal state.** There are none — each node has exactly one out-edge, so there is
no pair of writes whose order the policy must pin down and does not. No shared balance, cap or dedup
key is touched by two writes at the same level of the tree. The terminal state is unique:
`service_ledger` gains one `service_coverage_applied` row (−1587.01, `source_entry_id` =
`33a46ca9-…`) and one `service_rush_fee_charged` row (+448.17); `service_intake` gains one
`customer_confirmed` row (1422.57, effective 2026-09-17).

**No waiting.** Each resolving action is executable on the spot: write 1 needs only seeded records;
write 2 needs write 1's row plus the customer's immediate "yes"; write 3 needs write 2's row. The
customer is on the telephone and performs her own write during the call.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** Cited from `_difficulty.md` finding **F-8**: the three
tools this tree uses (`apply_claim_coverage_f28c459e`, `confirm_authorized_ceiling_b1b9df84`,
`charge_expedite_surcharge_af83d9eb`) each consist of a `ctx.make_id` call, one `ctx.create`, and a
return statement, with no branch, no raise, no status read and no conditional string. Calling
`charge_expedite_surcharge_af83d9eb` first would succeed silently — the environment makes the
agent's decision for it in neither direction.

**A customer's own write is in the tree.** `confirm_authorized_ceiling_b1b9df84` carries
`@tool(owner="user", rw="write")`, and the persona hands it over passively at the agent's direction
("when the agent hands the step over to her she carries it out herself and reads back what comes of
it"). She does not perform it unprompted and she does not perform the agent's writes.

**Isomorphic to the declared tree:** yes — same nodes, same two edges, same directions, same
`value_input` kinds, same gates.

### task_independent_derivation

**Now / wait / refuse: act now.** The order stands `in_workshop` (`status: "in_workshop"`), which is
where `service_authorization` permits bench labour and where the expedited surcharge attaches. Base
`service_expedited_handling` admits the promise only with at least the level's minimum notice:
Master Jeweler Service carries `minimum_notice_hours_for_rush: 48` and
`rush_turnaround_business_days: 4`; `frozen_time` is 2026-09-17 and the piece is wanted by
2026-10-03 — sixteen days, far beyond both. `same_day_service_available` is irrelevant (she is not
asking for same-day). Nothing requires a wait and nothing requires a refusal.

**The object.** One work order. The customer holds two:

- `196f5015-84e2-4dcc-9f30-47b76f45ba95` — Priority Bench Service, `delivered` 2024-11-16,
  `WO-402518`, a wedding band.

The persona names *"Her engagement ring, a platinum solitaire with a six-claw setting"*, left *"in the
middle of June"*, whose promised date *"has come and gone"*. That is `c73faeec-…` and only that.
Correlation key: `service_order_id` for the ledger rows, `item_sku` `RING-52704` for the
cross-category reads. The second order is excluded by description, by date and by status; every
history aggregate below is confined to `c73faeec-…` by the rule's own words ("standing priced on that
work order", "already stand charged on it").

**The user's need, authorisation boundary and timing.** She names the object (the engagement ring at
the workshop), the timing (before 3 October), and the mode: the desk may act at its own end
(*"you do whatever you need to do on your side"*) but the commitment with her name on it is hers
(*"she will not agree to anything open-ended… once she has heard it she says yes, and when the agent
hands the step over to her she carries it out herself"*). That is exactly the agent/customer split the
charter draws — two agent writes (the coverage credit, the surcharge) and one customer write (the
ceiling). She authorises the expedited charge in terms (*"if that's what it costs to have it for the
third, then go ahead"*). Nothing in GT's shape requires an authorisation she has not given, and
nothing she asks for falls outside it.

  `verify_customer_identity` — the persona supplies name, phone, `date_of_birth` 1984-03-22 and
  `identification_last_four` 3342, one at a time on request, matching `customers.b1a6fc32-…`.
- The work order: she has no reference (*"the yellow slip is somewhere in a kitchen drawer"*) and asks
  for it to be found under her name — `find_service_orders(customer_id=…)` returns both orders and the
  descriptions distinguish them.

All are `owner="agent", rw="read"` tools in `blueprint/share_tools.py`. No policy input and no

simulator; and the one figure she carries in her head (what she paid in June, −800.00 on 2026-06-25)
matches the record, so persona and DB do not conflict.

## findings

**T0-1 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED`: coverage applied on a claim that stands filed but has not been
accepted.**
*Symptom.* The task's first scored write books a protection credit for claim `CL-330871`, which the
protection register shows as filed and undecided. A base clause still in force forbids exactly that.
*Root cause.* The undeclared override recorded as `_difficulty.md` **F-1**:
`service_ext_claim_coverage_credit.overwrite` supersedes only the sentence about *the amount*, leaving
base's two eligibility sentences inherited, and the extended rule's opening sentence weakens them from
*accepted* to *filed and not refused*.
*Evidence.*
- `initial_state.protection_ledger.7bdd809f-30bb-4398-873d-6252a9068239`:
  `event_type: "protection_claim_filed"`, `claim_reference: "CL-330871"`, `posted_date: "2026-09-05"`,
  `claim_outcome: "not_applicable"`. No `protection_claim_settled` and no `protection_claim_denied`
  row carries `CL-330871`.
- base `service_protection_coverage.rule`: *"Where no protection claim has been accepted the desk does
  not take the amount off in anticipation of one, because the claim decision is the protection desk's
  to make and not this one's."*
- The GT's own proof field repeats the conflation rather than resolving it:
  `solvability_contract.gold_actions[0].base_preconditions[0]` quotes the base condition *"Coverage is
  applied only against the priced line it answers for, identified by the claim reference and **the
  work order entry the claim was accepted for**"* and records `"satisfied": true`, while the evidence
  it cites for that gate includes
  `initial_state.service_ledger.33a46ca9-….protection_claim_reference`, whose seeded value is the
  empty string `""`. No row anywhere in the world records an acceptance of `CL-330871`.
  `gold_actions[0].request_binding.action_semantics` likewise writes *"the workshop's own rule says
  what an **accepted** claim answers for is taken off the order"* about a claim that has only been
  filed.
*Demonstrated consequence.* Two defensible readings and two different scored values on every one of
this task's three writes: applying the credit gives 1587.01 / 1422.57 / 448.17; declining to apply it
in anticipation of a decision gives no credit, a ceiling of 3743.56 and a surcharge of 907.72
(recomputed in `### policy_self_consistency`).
*Affected artifact and location.*
`env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/workshop_service_desk/service.extended.yaml`,
`extended_policies[0] service_ext_claim_coverage_credit` — `overwrite` (incomplete) and `rule`

**T0-3 — `SOURCE-CHAIN RED`: the closure's load-bearing demonstration for the coverage edge is not a

*Symptom.* `prerequisite_closure` asserts that skipping the coverage credit recomputes the ceiling to
3339.53 and the expedited charge to 1052.95. Neither figure is what the policy produces on this world,
and the two are not consistent with each other.
*Root cause.* The counterfactual was not recomputed through the charter's own ladders; the asserted
ceiling and the asserted downstream charge were produced independently and never reconciled.
*Evidence.*
- `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1].skipped_effect`: *"Skipping the coverage credit leaves
  the bench total the customer is answering for at 2559.70 instead of 972.69, and the ceiling
  recomputes to 3339.53 instead of 1422.57, which in turn carries the expedited charge to 1052.95."*
- `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness` repeats it: *"taking the authorisation first gives a ceiling
  of 3339.53 built on a bench total of 2559.70"*.
- Recomputation on the named world (bench total 2559.70, every factor at the tier this world puts the
  customer on — `delay_contingency_rate` 20, `stale_figure_step` 5, `member_standing_step` 3,
  `covered_work_step` 9 since `remaining_benefit_allowance` 2800.00 ≥ 2559.70,
  `bench_clock_anchor` 30 days, `delay_allowance_uplift` ×1.25):
  `allowance = RND(2559.70 × 37/100, 2) = 947.09`; `uplifted = RND(947.09 × 1.25, 2) = 1183.86`;
  ceiling = `RND(2559.70 + 1183.86, 2)` = **3743.56**. Then
  `base_amount = RND(3743.56 × 22/100, 2) = 823.58`;
  `relieved = RND((823.58 + 185.00) × 90/100, 2) = 907.72`;
  `cap = RND(3743.56 × 40/100, 2) = 1497.42`; surcharge = **907.72**.
- An exhaustive sweep of every legal combination of this policy's own ladder tiers
  (`contingency ∈ {20,12,6}`, `stale ∈ {10,5,0}`, `member ∈ {6,3,0}`, `covered ∈ {9,4,0}`,
  `uplift ∈ {1.5,1.25,1.0}`) under both half-to-even-on-decimal and float rounding produces **no**
  ceiling within a cent of 3339.53.
- The two asserted figures contradict each other: 1052.95 as an expedited charge requires a ceiling of
  4476.98 (`RND(4476.98 × 22/100, 2) = 984.94`; `RND((984.94 + 185.00) × 90/100, 2) = 1052.95`), not
  3339.53 — from which the charge would be 827.73.
*Demonstrated consequence.* The proof the artifact submits for the load-bearing character of the
`revised_authorization → claim_coverage_credit` edge does not hold: the figures it offers as "what
skipping this step gives" are not what skipping this step gives. (The edge *is* load-bearing — my own
recomputation shows 1422.57 → 3743.56 and 448.17 → 907.72 — but reaching the same conclusion is not
the same as the submitted proof holding, and a reader who checks the closure against the world finds
it false.) Recorded under the problem-tree relationship, which these sentences exist to support.
*Affected artifact and location.* `tasks/0.json` —
`prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1].skipped_effect` and
`prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness`. No scored parameter is affected.
*Relation to previous revisions.* First revision.

recomputation, it is the only tie in either task, and the relationship it supports is untouched — the

rather than a red light on that ground; a reader who holds the charter's stated convention to be
binding on every figure would upgrade it.
*Affected artifact and location.* `tasks/0.json`,
`computations[1].factor_sensitivity[1].baseline_result` and `computations[1].factor_trace[1]`.
